keyFindings.description: Finding 1 holds for a rules refusal only. A block-mode charter revise still counts `breakerThings(callAsks())`, the upload's full scan with the blocks its stored version holds, so two charter refusals of uploads that each add a different new ask beside a stored #window trip #window, and a third upload's new ask goes out with outcome breaker, judged by neither check. Both thermonuclear reviews reproduced it with the PR's three-upload test under bySystem(REVISE, RULES_NONE): entries verdict/revise/none, verdict/revise/none, breaker/allow.

Finding 5's fix holds, but half of it has no test: with the in-flight cut (`for (const stop of recordStops) stop.abort(RECORD_SHUT_DOWN)`) made a no-op, the PR's shutdown test still passes, because its record starts after shutdown; a record already in flight when shutdown begins then keeps its 5 s stop and its entry is lost (both reviews' probe: returnedAt 1500, entries []; at head returnedAt 1250 with the entry).

fixesHold.2_envoy_nudge: Holds: pi-shared withoutComment drops a trailing comment where bash ends the line; envoy.test.ts's rebutted-command case passes and fails with withoutComment a no-op; pi-shared's bash differential test passes with bash present.
fixesHold.3_resend_unreadable: Holds: overrideComment reads a trailing comment of override flags alone as the rebuttal, every other comment stays unreadable; the deep review's differential fuzz of 5,547 commands against real bash 5.2 found 0 mismatches for AskGate's 352 scoped and the shared scan's 2,048 accepted commands.
fixesHold.4_refusal_texts: Holds: both renderers use the per-surface `fate`; the test fails with the old texts restored.
fixesHold.5_shutdown_entry: Holds at head (entry written by 1,250 ms); its in-flight half is untested (finding above).

newPaths: No new way an ask reaches the person unjudged: an accepted comment is override flags alone, so it is the rebuttal the flag already gave, recorded as one; comment text is cut before here-document detection; tripped and revised use the same identities (judged is a filter of the same scan, and a retype's identity ignores the opening readAsks rewrites). One narrower record loss, judged not a defect: a Dispatch record that answers 250-500 ms after a call given up at the end of the shutdown grace is now cut where it used to land; the entry still lands and names the cut in recordError, and the README says when the stop comes.
